impacts.claim: Train B changes release governance, UAT evidence, recovery, upgrade discovery, upgrade planning, guarded apply, validation, packaging, and traceability.
impacts.evidence: DEC-009 and the approved roadmap explicitly combine former v0.8 and v0.9 into one v0.8.0 train.
impacts.next_verification: Review the final Train B diff and feature-to-evidence matrix before UAT handoff.

impacts.claim: New tools remain Python standard-library only; optional upstream discovery depends on local packages or configured GitHub release metadata, while offline fixtures cover the same contract.
impacts.evidence: The existing package and automation tools use standard-library-only implementations and fail closed around unavailable external systems.
impacts.next_verification: Run compile checks, dependency inspection, offline fixtures, and an optional read-only GitHub metadata check.

impacts.claim: Upgrade planning compares project-specific files and may encounter private audit, runtime, or Agent context, so reports must contain hashes/classifications rather than raw private content and apply must be path-confined.
impacts.evidence: Existing safety policies classify local, team, private, and public artifacts and prohibit output of matched values or source content.
impacts.next_verification: Test protected paths, traversal refusal, sanitized reports/receipts, and run private staged plus public tracked safety scans.

impacts.claim: Release, rollback, upgrade, startup, quality gates, UAT, examples, and operator prompts must describe the new inspect-plan-approve-apply-verify lifecycle consistently.
impacts.evidence: The current roadmap and UPGRADE_POLICY define the intended behavior but do not yet provide executable Train B controls.
impacts.next_verification: Run strict validator and an Owner walkthrough of release and upgrade quick paths.

impacts.claim: Release-state and file-migration safety claims require deterministic offline tests for evidence gates, conflicts, freshness, authorization, path confinement, idempotency, preservation, package extraction, and failure recovery.
impacts.evidence: Train A established focused unit tests, strict validation, deterministic packaging, and extracted-package verification as release evidence.
impacts.next_verification: Run focused release/upgrade suites, the complete source suite, delayed package comparison, and the complete extracted-package suite.

impacts.claim: Only the Owner can confirm that lifecycle wording, release readiness, recovery guidance, conflict explanations, preservation behavior, and upgrade controls are understandable and trustworthy.
impacts.evidence: DEC-009 requires one consolidated Train B UAT and RELEASE_POLICY forbids Codex self-acceptance.
impacts.next_verification: Prepare a bilingual v0.8.0 UAT with explicit actions and expected results, then stop for the Owner conclusion.

impacts.claim: Train B changes the mechanism that plans OS upgrades and release recovery, so rollout must be branch-based and rollback must preserve the last accepted package plus project-specific memory without destructive automation.
impacts.evidence: The existing release policy uses immutable GitHub tags/assets and UPGRADE_POLICY lists files that must never be overwritten automatically.
impacts.next_verification: Dogfood an isolated older-to-candidate upgrade, simulate verification failure, verify protected hashes, and inspect rollback guidance before UAT.

test_plan: Compile all source and template Python tools.
Run focused lifecycle/release readiness tests and focused upgrade planner/apply tests.
Test missing UAT/safety/package/rollback evidence and contradictory release states.
Test version comparison, identical/upstream/local/both-modified files, protected paths, traversal, stale plans, authorization, idempotency, and verification failure.
Dogfood an older packaged OS to the v0.8.0 candidate in an isolated temporary repository.
Run strict source/template validation and private/public safety gates.
Build two delayed deterministic packages, extract one, and run the full extracted-package suite.
uat_plan: Owner distinguishes code complete, review complete, UAT Pass, released, and post-release done from generated evidence.
Owner reviews a READY release plan and at least one BLOCKED plan with a clear next action.
Owner follows rollback/hotfix/post-release guidance and confirms no destructive action is automatic.
Owner reviews installed/upstream version discovery and an upgrade conflict report.
Owner verifies LOCAL_OVERRIDES, audit/Linear records, safety dispositions, and private/runtime context survive the dogfood upgrade.
Owner gives an explicit pass or fail conclusion for v0.8.0.
rollout: Implement on codex/v0.8-train-b, keep all remote/destructive operations manual, prepare a Draft PR and deterministic candidate package, then stop for explicit v0.8.0 human UAT before merge, tag, or Release.
rollback: Before release, abandon the Train B branch. After release, reinstall the immutable v0.6.0 package or the latest accepted package on a new branch while preserving LOCAL_OVERRIDES, audit history, Linear mappings, safety dispositions, runtime/private context, and human UAT records.
